title: Patsy at the Dew Drop and the blues singers of the day
summary: The blues singers of the era and the performer Patsy, who chose to be announced as man or woman at the Dew Drop.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I can't think of Tip-A-Lite's name now. Uh-huh. But anyhow, he sang the blues. In those days, the blues singers was Tip-A-Lite, Joe August, who was named Google Eyes, Roy Brown, Fats Domino was just getting started. Um, Lloyd Ignatius, um, um, Patsy Vildar was the toast of the town. Yeah, sure. Miss Patsy. Yeah, well, you see, when I played at the do drop for Frank, and so forth, and I used to sometimes do the announcing about who was coming up. But before you get started on the night, before the night started, you would ask Pat, or Patsy, what you want tonight? Pat? Pat? Okay.
Uh, reel number three with Milton Batiste on February 5th, 1997. Okay.

So, to finish telling you about Patsy, you know, uh, when Patsy would come in at night, I'd meet him at the door, so forth, so on. Say, uh, well, what you want tonight? Pat? A Patsy? And, uh, it's according to how he felt, you know, whether he wanted to be introduced that night as a man or a woman. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. So, on those nights that he wanted to be a woman, we bring you the toast of the town, Patsy Bildaya. Yeah. You know, and on the manly night, it was Pat.
